source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); Line 8 subtractions, a closed list (PDF p.10); 'Utah residents who earn income in other states' (PDF p.7)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = public pension paid by NY (person 0) 60,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 44,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (single): line 4 federal AGI 60,000.00. Line 5 additions: none, 0.00. Line 6 = 60,000.00 + 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 60,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 10 = 60,000.00 x 0.045 = 2,700.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 15,750.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 60,000.00, cap 15,750.00) = 0.06 x 15,750.00 = 945.00. Line 17 base phase-out amount 18,213.00. Line 18 = max(0, 60,000.00 - 18,213.00) = 41,787.00. Line 19 = 41,787.00 x 0.013 = 543.231. Line 20 = max(0, 945.00 - 543.231) = 401.769. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 60,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 15,750.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 15,750.00; line 5 = max(0, 60,000.00 - 15,750.00) = 44,250.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 401.769 = 401.769; credits 401.77. Tax = 2,700.00 - 401.77 = 2,298.23. New York State pension: Line 8 is a closed list of nine subtractions (PDF p.10) and none is a government pension; Utah prints no rule by paying state, so this pension stays in federal AGI on line 4 and is taxed like any income ('Utah residents who earn income in other states must pay Utah tax on that income', PDF p.7). Expected lines are the formula results rounded to the cent at the end (half up); the three-decimal figures above are unrounded.
